name: Training Data Store & Fine-Tuning Pipeline
description: Manages the full lifecycle of training data collection, storage, fine-tuning orchestration, model validation, and promotion. This is the component that turns remote API responses into local model capability. Designed as a thin orchestration facade with three injected dependencies (training_data_store, fine_tuning_orchestrator, model_validator) and a small, high-level API surface. The pipeline does NOT re-export sub-component methods — it wraps them in orchestrated workflows. Data version is a hash computed at pipeline run start, tying the run to a specific data snapshot. Budget check happens before fine-tuning starts. Consecutive validation failures are tracked and surfaced in status/logs. State is persisted as JSON for resumability. Structured JSON logging at every decision point for auditability.

fields.description: Day of month when the budget resets (1-28). Values above 28 are not allowed to avoid month-length ambiguity.

types.description: Budget constraints for the pipeline. Budget enforcement is hard — the system stops spending, never exceeds limits. Projected cost is compared against remaining budget before fine-tuning starts.

types.name: PipelineTriggerPolicy

fields.name: min_new_examples
fields.description: Minimum number of new training examples (since last successful run) required before triggering. Must be at least 1.

fields.name: min_interval_seconds
fields.description: Minimum time in seconds between pipeline runs. Prevents rapid re-triggering. 0.0 disables cooldown.

fields.name: max_consecutive_failures
fields.description: Maximum consecutive pipeline failures before trigger is suppressed until manual reset. After this threshold, should_trigger() returns false and logs at ERROR level.

fields.name: confidence_ceiling
fields.description: If the current local model's aggregate confidence score already exceeds this ceiling, skip fine-tuning (diminishing returns). Set to 1.0 to disable.

functions.name: initialize
functions.description: Initializes the TrainingPipeline with the given configuration and injected dependencies. Creates the state file directory if needed, loads persisted state from JSON (or creates fresh state if no state file exists), initializes the training data store dependency, checks for incomplete runs from a prior crash (marks them as FAILED), and reconciles budget period tracking. Must be called before any other method. Fails fast on invalid configuration per project standards.

functions.name: should_trigger
functions.description: Evaluates the trigger policy against the current pipeline state and returns a detailed TriggerEvaluation. Checks: (1) sufficient new examples since last successful run, (2) minimum interval since last run, (3) consecutive failure count below threshold, (4) budget remaining, (5) confidence ceiling not already exceeded, (6) pipeline not currently running. All checks are logged for auditability. This is a read-only evaluation — no state is mutated.

functions.name: run_pipeline
functions.description: Executes the full pipeline: DATA_SNAPSHOT → BUDGET_CHECK → FINE_TUNE → VALIDATE → PROMOTE. This is the main orchestration method. Acquires an async lock to prevent concurrent runs. On each step: updates the PipelineRun record, persists state, and logs. On any step failure: marks remaining steps as SKIPPED, persists the failed run, increments consecutive failure count, and returns PipelineFailure. On success: resets consecutive failure count, updates active model version, and returns PipelineSuccess. Budget is checked before fine-tuning starts — if projected cost exceeds remaining budget, the run is skipped with SKIPPED_BUDGET status. The pipeline is resumable: on restart after a crash, initialize() marks incomplete runs as FAILED.

invariants: No exceptions are raised past the public interface boundary for expected failure conditions — all expected failures (insufficient data, validation regression, budget exhausted, fine-tuning failure) are represented as PipelineFailure in PipelineResult.

Only RuntimeError (not_initialized, already_running), ValueError (config/validation errors at construction), IOError (unrecoverable I/O), and TypeError (dependency protocol mismatch) may be raised as exceptions.
Pipeline runs are serialized: at most one run_pipeline() execution is active at any time, enforced by an asyncio.Lock. Attempting a concurrent run raises RuntimeError.
PipelineState is persisted to the state file after every state transition (step completion, failure, status change). On crash and restart, initialize() recovers the last persisted state.

Consecutive failure count is incremented on every pipeline run that ends in FAILED status, and reset to 0 on every run that ends in COMPLETED status. It is never modified by other operations except reset_consecutive_failures().
PipelineRun.steps always contains exactly 5 PipelineStepRecord entries — one per PipelineStepName — in the canonical order: DATA_SNAPSHOT, BUDGET_CHECK, FINE_TUNE, VALIDATE, PROMOTE.
If a step fails, all subsequent steps in the run are marked SKIPPED (not PENDING).

Budget enforcement is hard: if current_month_spent_usd + estimated_cost_per_run_usd > max_monthly_budget_usd, the run is immediately rejected with SKIPPED_BUDGET status before any fine-tuning resources are consumed.
Budget period resets are computed against budget_reset_day: when the current UTC date's day >= budget_reset_day and the last reset was in a prior period, current_month_spent_usd is set to 0.0.

DataSnapshot.data_version_hash is computed as SHA-256 over the sorted, concatenated input strings of all training examples for the task type at snapshot time. This makes the hash deterministic and independent of insertion order.
The pipeline never mutates the currently serving model on failure — if any step after fine-tuning fails (validation, promotion), the previous model version continues serving.
All structured log entries within a pipeline run include the same run_id as a correlation field.
No global mutable state: all state is scoped to the pipeline instance, its PipelineState, and its injected dependencies.
Config parsing is strict — all PipelineConfig validation happens at construction/initialization time. Invalid config causes immediate ValueError, never silently defaults.
PipelineRun records in run_history are pruned to run_history_limit after each run. Oldest runs are removed first.
add_example() never auto-triggers a pipeline run. Callers must check trigger_evaluation.should_trigger and call run_pipeline() explicitly.
PipelineResult is a discriminated union on the 'status' field: 'success' resolves to PipelineSuccess, 'failure' resolves to PipelineFailure.
